transcript.text: Good morning.
If you woke up already tired, before the day has even begun, stay with me for the next few minutes.
God has not run out of strength, and this morning he wants to give some of it to you.
Take one slow breath with me.
You do not have to pretend you are full of energy.
You can come to him exactly as you are: the heavy eyes, the long list, the worry you carried to bed and found waiting for you when you woke.
Let your shoulders drop.
Unclench your hands.
For the next few minutes, nothing is required of you except to listen and to let him lift what you cannot lift alone.
The prophet Isaiah wrote these words to people who were exhausted.
But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Notice the word renew.
You are not asked to manufacture strength out of nothing.
You are invited to receive it again, the way a field receives rain.
Waiting on the Lord is not doing nothing.
It is turning toward him first, before the phone, before the news, before the noise, and letting him set the pace of your day.
So let us begin honestly.
Lord, here I am.
You know how I slept, and you know how I feel.
I will not hide my tiredness from you.
I wait on you this morning.
Renew my strength.
Not the strength to do everything, but the strength to do the next right thing, and then the one after that.
Isaiah says it again, just two verses earlier.
He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
Look at who receives the power.
Not the strong.
Not the people who have it all together.
The faint.
The ones with no might left.
If that describes you this morning, you are not disqualified.
You are exactly the person this promise was written for.
David prayed like this at the start of his days.
My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.
Lord, like David, I direct my prayer to you before anything else.
Hear my voice this morning.
I lift my eyes from the problems in front of me and I look up.
Remind me that you are above this day, and that nothing in it will surprise you.

transcript.text: Jesus said, Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
The rest Jesus offers is not only for the end of the day.
It is a rest you can carry into the middle of it.
You can be busy and still be at rest on the inside, because the weight is no longer on your shoulders alone.
He is yoked beside you, pulling with you.
Lord, I bring you my work today.
The tasks I enjoy and the ones I have been putting off.
The conversations I need to have.
The people who depend on me.
Give me focus and diligence.
Help me to do good work, honestly and well, and to leave the results with you.
When I am tempted to rush, slow me down.
When I am tempted to give up, keep me going.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.
Father, there are parts of today I already know I cannot handle on my own.
I name them before you now, quietly, in my heart.
Instead of pretending, I admit my weakness.
And I ask you to meet me right there, in the place where I run out.
The apostle Paul heard this answer when he begged for his weakness to be taken away.
My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
God did not remove Paul's weakness.
He filled it.
The place where Paul ran out became the place where Christ's power showed up most clearly.
So your weakness this morning is not the end of the story.
It may be the exact spot where God plans to show you what he can do.
Lord, I lift up the people I love.
Those who share my home, and those who are far away.
Give them strength for their own days.
Protect them as they go out and as they come back.
Where there is tension between us, soften our hearts.
Help me to be patient and kind with them, even when I am tired.
And Lord, I pray for everyone listening to this prayer who is carrying more than usual.
The caregivers who were up in the night.
The parents of newborns.
The ones grieving.
The ones working two jobs.
The ones waiting for news.
Meet each of them this morning with exactly the strength they need for today.
My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
Father, I trust you with what I need today.
The bills, the groceries, the plans that depend on money I do not yet see.
You know every need before I speak it.
Provide what is necessary, and give me wisdom with what I already have.
Keep me from fear, and keep me generous.
Lord, there are choices in front of me today, some small and some that feel very big.
I do not want to make them in a hurry or out of fear.
Give me wisdom.
Close the doors that should be closed and open the ones you have prepared.
And if I cannot see the whole path, give me light enough for the next step.
Father, if I am carrying a grudge into this day, I lay it down before you.
You know the words that still sting and the person I keep replaying in my mind.
I do not have to pretend it did not hurt.
But I choose not to let it drain the strength you are giving me.
Help me to forgive as you have forgiven me, and to speak with grace today.
The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him.
Strength for what is inside you. A shield for what comes at you from outside.
God offers both in the same sentence.
And notice the order: my heart trusted, and I am helped.
Trust comes first. The help follows.
Lord, cover my home today.
Watch over the door as it opens and closes.
Keep every person who lives here safe on the road, at school, at work,
